headline: Gage Park anchors Ward 15, independent on business, weak on civic turnout.
summary:
Independent restaurants and grocers dominate here in Ward 15, with chain restaurant share ranking 2nd of 50 citywide at just over 19 percent of licensed restaurants. This pairing sits inside a ward that finishes 42nd of 50 overall, well below the city's midpoint. Ward 15 stretches across New City, Gage Park, West Englewood, and Chicago Lawn on the Southwest Side. Coffee shops here also rate among the best in Chicago, and voter turnout runs low, with just over 22 percent of registered voters casting ballots in the most recent municipal election, one of the lower turnout rates in the city.

Ride-share spending and recorded real estate sales both sit near the bottom of the fifty wards, and residents report some of the lowest rates of physical activity and everyday contact with neighbors anywhere in Chicago.
reading_the_rankings: Two of the ward's strongest marks come from business licensing data. Local restaurants and grocers dominate the count, with chain restaurant share ranked 2nd of 50 at 19.05 percent of licensed restaurants, and major chain store share ranked 2nd as well, at 1.79 percent of licensed food stores. Both figures are tied to the ward boundary as it stood when the license was recorded, and before 2023 this was a differently shaped ward, so some of the older records describe a boundary that no longer exists. The agency behind this data puts its own confidence at medium, not high, and the licensing tally behind both measures doesn't reach every one of the fifty wards either. The ward also ranks 2nd on non-routine bills sponsored by alders associated with it this council session, 206 in total, a count of legislative activity tied to the ward rather than a measure of any one official's output. That number carries the same before-2023 boundary caveat as the business data. On the softer end, the ward ranks 49th of 50 on the modeled share of adults who talk or spend time with neighbors at least monthly, which this dataset puts at 0 percent. This figure comes from a model built on a national survey and pushed down to the ward level, not from anyone actually counting conversations on the block, and the group behind the estimate calls its own confidence low. So the number says more about how Ward 15 compares to the other forty-nine than about any specific count of actual conversations.

news.headline: Pedestrian killed in Gage Park crash
news.note: A 63-year-old man was fatally struck by a speeding SUV that lost control in the 5100 block of South Western Avenue, inside the ward.
